title: Ironpeak Systems - Activation Orientation & Runbook Handoff
summary: Kickoff for Ironpeak's activation: onboarding runbook review, networking and security intake (VPC, SSO), staging API access, and pilot success criteria. Action items assigned for docs, SSO setup, and a small benchmark in staging. Some discussion about dedicated vs hosted capacity and expected throughput/latency constraints.
action_items: Lina Carrasco - Send activation runbook PDF + SSO checklist - due 2026-02-18
Priya Nair - Share VPC CIDR and existing peering contacts (AWS account IDs) - due 2026-02-17
Joan Kim - Provision staging API key and run quick latency/cost sample with their sample traces - due 2026-02-20
Nadia Romero - Confirm SOC2 report access and list of compliance questions - due 2026-02-19
next_steps: Redwood to share runbook and security pack
Customer to provide VPC details and SSO metadata
Schedule 30-min staging benchmark with SEs next week
Set up pilot kickoff meeting (week of 2/23)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Lina, Samir, Joan (Redwood) — Markus, Priya, Evan, Nadia (Ironpeak)

[00:00] Lina: Okay everyone thanks for joining — happy valentines day if you're, uh, celebrating. quick intro, I'm Lina, i'll run the activation side, Samir our CSM will coordinate acceptance criteria, and Joan is our SE who will help with staging and the benchmark. Markus?
[00:12] Markus: Hey thanks Lina, we're excited. quick context: Ironpeak is doing an internal pilot that surfaces LLM powered search and summarization across logs, so low latency for 512 token-ish responses is the big ask. timeline: want pilot in staging in two weeks, production in six.
[00:28] Samir: Great, that's helpful. short list of success criteria we heard from email: under 200ms p50 for short queries, cost target around $0.003 per 1k tokens (rough target), and traceability — audit logs and retention to meet internal controls.
[00:44] Priya: yep, and we have network constraints: everything must go through our VPC, no egress from staging unless approved, and SSO required. we may be in a private deployment but we want to evaluate hosted first.
[00:58] Joan: thanks, that's totally in scope. quick note — "hosted" can do staging quickly with VPC peering and private endpoints, Dedicated offers predictable throughput if you want reserved GPUs. there's a tradeoff: dedicated lowers variance and tail latency but requires committment.
[01:15] Evan: can you expand on the latency tradeoffs — are we likely to see big jumps on peak?
[01:20] Joan: sure. For small request volumes hosted is fine; variability comes from multi-tenant scheduling and cold starts for large context. we use continuous batching and KV cache to reduce per-token compute — the KV cache is unlikely to help for single-shot summaries, but prefix cache helps for repeated contexts. also note quantization profiles can reduce cost but might slightly affect quality.
[01:45] Nadia: from security side we need to see SOC2 and have the ability to rotate keys via our KMS; audit logs need to capture request id, model version, and user token mapping for 90 days.
[01:58] Lina: noted. we'll share our security pack and SOC2 attestation. on key management we integrate with customer KMS via envelope encryption for Private, and for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys in certain tiers.
[02:12] Markus: what's the path for on-prem? we have stricter data rules for some PII logs.
[02:18] Joan: Private deployment (VPC/on-prem option) is absolutely an option — it takes longer to provision (3–6 weeks typically), but it's the right move for air-gapped or regulated data. for the pilot i'd suggest hosted with VPC peering to get fast feedback and then move to Private/Dedicated if compliance gates require it.
[02:36] Priya: sounds pragmatic. So immediate asks: runbook, SSO metadata, and a staging API key. we'll provide VPC details.
[02:44] Samir: i'll capture that as next steps. Joan, can you walk through the runbook highlights?
[02:49] Joan: sure. runbook sections: access and onboarding (who gets API keys), network setup (CIDRs, peering, firewall rules), SSO/SAML config and mapping to RBAC, test harness for latency/cost, rollout plan (canary, A/B, automatic fallback to cheaper model variant), and troubleshooting.
[03:12] [03:15] Speaker 1: (overlap) also included are observability steps — per-route token cost breakdown, per-model latency histograms, and error sampling.
[03:22] Joan: right, we put sample dashboards in the pack — you'll get token-level cost and p50/p95 latency.
[03:29] Markus: any gotchas on peering? we run in AWS in us-east-1.
[03:33] Joan: we support cross-account VPC peering and PrivateLink. we'll need your AWS account IDs and CIDR ranges. if you want strict egress control we can route through our private endpoints so no public egress. Occasionally customers forget to open the ephemeral ports used by our runtime — we'll call that out.
[03:50] Priya: okay i'll send CIDRs and account ids after the call.
[03:53] Evan: about the staging benchmark — what does Redwood need from us?
[03:57] Joan: a sample workload and a small set of representative prompts. ideally 500–1k requests to get a stable p95. we can run with your dataset or a redacted sample. we'll produce a latency/cost spreadsheet.
[04:10] [04:12] Lina: action: Joan will provision a staging API key and run the quick benchmark with Evan.
[04:17] Evan: quick Q — do you support streaming and function calling patterns? our summarization uses streaming to push tokens as they arrive.
[04:25] Joan: yes streaming supported; function calling is supported as well but requires some mapping on your end for the tool schema. streaming does increase open connection count; for high concurrency we recommend tuned autoscale on Dedicated.
[04:40] Nadia: on encryption — we need confirmation of in-transit and at-rest, and whether metadata such as user id is stored by Redwood.
[04:48] Lina: all data in transit is TLS, at rest is AES-256, and metadata retention policies are configurable; we do collect request ids for observability but can disable storing raw inputs in hosted mode if needed — though that limits debugability.
[05:05] Markus: what's the ramp plan after pilot? if pilot looks good do we do a 3 month dedicated commit?
[05:11] Samir: typically customers evaluate pilot metrics and then choose Dedicated for production to get consistent SLOs. we can prepare a cost model showing currency of cost per token at various commit levels.
[05:22] Priya: please include pre-quantization and post-quantization results.
[05:25] Joan: will do. we'll run both FP16 and 8-bit quant profiles in the sample and show the quality delta.
[05:33] [05:36] Speaker 2: slight transcription glitch — said "8-byte" earlier — meant 8-bit.
[05:39] Nadia: for compliance we'll need an inventory of logs and how long each type is stored.
[05:44] Lina: noted; i'll include the retention matrix in the security pack.
[05:48] Markus: any contract/legal points we should be aware of before pilot?
[05:51] Samir: pilot can run under a standard evaluation agreement; if you need DPA or additional clauses we'll route to legal, timeline for legal review usually 1–2 weeks.
[06:02] Priya: is there a staging tier in Redwood Console we can use for team access?
[06:06] Joan: yes we can create a staging tenant with RBAC; we'll give DevOps admin, and read-only to product for observability. SSO mapping to groups takes a bit of initial config.
[06:16] Evan: how do rollbacks work if model quality regresses post-rollout?
[06:20] Joan: we have automatic fallback policies — you can specify model variant fallbacks, and canary windows. Console exposes drift alerts tied to your evals so if a quality regression triggers we can rollback to a pinned model.
[06:34] Markus: perfect. can you show the sample of the canary config in the runbook?
[06:38] Joan: yes it's in the rollout section, short example: 5% traffic for 30 minutes then 25% for 1 hour, with automatic rollback on metric threshold breach.
[06:49] [07:00] Lina: all right let's talk logistics: Samir will be main contact for acceptance criteria; Priya will handle network; Nadia security; Evan will be the questions-to-SE person. we'll set a brief follow-up next week for the staging benchmark.
[07:12] Priya: one more thing — do you support IP allowlists for the connectors?
[07:15] Joan: yes, static egress IPs are available for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we can provide a set of egress ranges but they can change with major infra changes — we'll call that out.
[07:29] Markus: can we get an ETA on the runbook and the security pack?
[07:32] Lina: we'll share both within 2 business days, so expect them by Tues 2/17.
[07:37] [07:40] Evan: quick note on dataset — we'll scrub PII and provide a sample around 1k items; is that sufficient?
[07:46] Joan: yep that's perfect for the first pass.
[07:49] Nadia: do you support customer-managed keys with AWS KMS for hosted? you mentioned envelope earlier.
[07:54] Lina: yes under our higher tier we support CMK via envelope encryption; we'll include the setup steps in the security pack.
[08:02] Samir: next steps recap: runbook and security pack from Redwood, VPC details and SSO metadata from Ironpeak, staging dataset from Evan. Joan to provision staging key and run benchmark; schedule 30m follow-up.
[08:17] Markus: sounds good.
[08:20] Lina: any last questions?
[08:22] [08:25] Speaker 3: (minor crosstalk)
[08:27] Priya: not from me.
[08:29] Evan: no, thanks.
[08:30] Lina: great thanks everyone, we'll send notes and action items after this and look to meet week of 2/23 for pilot kickoff if staging results look good.
[08:42] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript: occasional ASR errors (e.g., "8-bit" -> "8-byte", "KV cache" mis-transcribed as "KV cash" in earlier audio), speaker overlaps present.
